page: Amazon Web Services p5.48xlarge is a flagship accelerated computing instance designed for distributed deep learning and large-scale parallel processing. The server is powered by AMD x86_64 processors operating at 3.6 GHz, offering 192 vCPUs distributed across 96 dedicated physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system incorporates 2048.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 10.67 GB of RAM per physical core, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture.

The core accelerator subsystem comprises eight NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs delivering a collective total of 640 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM. For high-throughput local caching, dataset staging, and checkpointing, the instance integrates 30,400 GB of NVMe SSD local storage. Extreme interconnectivity is provided by a baseline network bandwidth of 3200 Gbps, enabling multi-node cluster scaling without common data transfer bottlenecks.

This hardware footprint represents an ultra-high-density compute profile where cost efficiency is achieved through massive throughput and rapid completion times for deep learning training and large language model inference rather than modest baseline operating costs. The primary architectural tradeoff is the sheer scale of the system, which requires specialized workloads capable of saturating 8 H100 GPUs, hundreds of gigabits of bandwidth, and hundreds of virtual CPU cores.

Appropriate workload fits for the p5.48xlarge include large-scale generative AI model pre-training, complex multi-node distributed training, low-latency large language model serving, high-performance scientific simulations, and extreme-scale ETL or data transformation pipelines.
